purpose: Scoped cover-production authority for Stardust Station. Makes the released Issue 1 cover available as a pixel-read trade-dress anchor while leaving issue-specific cover composition to the assembled RexPrompt cover recipe.

rules: Before generating any Stardust Station cover, retrieve and visually inspect the actual pixels of the local Issue 1 cover trade-dress reference. Repository path, SHA, metadata or remembered appearance are not substitutes for pixel readback.

The Issue 1 cover reference controls series masthead lettering architecture, Star Splitter Visions publisher bug, issue-number placement, overall cover-brand rhythm, polished animated-comic rendering, and broad blue-violet/cyan StarTrust visual identity.
The Issue 1 cover reference does NOT control later-cover scene composition, cast count, staging, focal object, issue-specific palette accents, or story hook.
The assembled current cover recipe controls the selling image, cast, environment, composition, focal hierarchy, spoiler ceiling and exact issue-specific text.
Released Stardust Station interior pages and approved visual-reference-pack entries control character identity, station design and established world appearance.
Do not use any cover, including Issue 1, as interior story-page layout authority.
Do not copy the Issue 1 ensemble-lineup composition onto later issues unless a later recipe explicitly requests an ensemble.

preserve: white masthead letterforms with dark blue depth/outline
cyan orbital swoosh and star/spark accents integrated around the masthead
Star Splitter Visions publisher bug in the upper-left region
ISSUE #N placement in the upper-right region
issue subtitle centered beneath the masthead when a canonical subtitle exists
allowIssueVariation: accent color within established Stardust palette
forbidden: fake action spectacle unrelated to the issue
unreadable environmental text used as a required story device
using the cover reference as interior-page layout authority

workflow: Resolve the selected Stardust cover show entry and assemble its exact cover recipe.
Retrieve the local Issue 1 cover reference as actual pixels and visually inspect it.
Retrieve the smallest relevant released/current visual references for characters and station elements named in the cover recipe.
Use the Issue 1 cover only for trade dress and brand continuity; use the current recipe for the actual cover concept.
Generate the cover, then audit thumbnail readability, masthead consistency, character/world continuity, spoiler ceiling and exact cover lettering.
